chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Hasan ibn Husayn al-Lu'lu'i from Safwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'Indeed, Hisham narrated from you that you ordered him to perform complete prayer (al-tamam) in the two Sanctuaries (Mecca and Medina), and that was for the sake of the people.' He said, 'No, it was I and those who preceded me from my fathers; when we entered Mecca, we completed the prayer and concealed ourselves from the people.'

And what we preceded with regarding that it is appropriate for one to combine (prayers) while staying for ten days, according to what we mentioned, is in the manner of recommendation (nadb) and preference (istihbab), not obligation (farḍ) and necessity (ijab). And whenever a person does not do it, it is permissible for him to perform complete prayer (al-itmam), indeed it is better. And that which indicates this is what he narrated:

key_terms.الاسْتِحْبَابِ: Recommendation or preference in Islamic jurisprudence, a level below obligation
key_terms.التَّمَامِ: Complete prayer (performing four rak'ahs of two-rak'ah prayers) while in the state of pilgrimage or in the Sanctuaries
key_terms.الْإِتْمَامُ: The act of completing the prayer
key_terms.الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two Sanctuaries, referring to Mecca and Medina

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and reason for performing complete prayer (al-tamam) in Mecca and Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the jurisprudential basis for performing *al-tamam* (complete four-rak'ah prayer) in the two Sanctuaries, attributing the practice to the consistent Sunnah of the Imams rather than mere concession for the public. It establishes that while staying for ten days to combine prayers is recommended (*istihbab*) rather than obligatory, performing the complete prayer remains permissible and preferable if the pilgrim does not remain for the full duration, reflecting the flexibility in Shia fiqh regarding Hajj rituals.
